candidates.title: Edmonton woman says she was ‘unpersoned’ by church after Orthodox clergyman charged with sexual assault
candidates.description: A member of the clergy with an Orthodox church in Edmonton has been accused of sexually assaulting a woman more than two decades ago, and the complainant in the case says she was ostracized from the church after reporting the alleged crime.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Minor cabinet shuffle Wednesday for P.E.I. Premier Rob Lantz
candidates.description: Prince Edward Island Premier Rob Lantz undertook a minor shakeup of his executive council Wednesday afternoon at Government House in Charlottetown.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ethics watchdog finds Liberal MP Idlout violated conflict of interest code
candidates.description: Ottawa's ethics commissioner found Liberal MP Lori Idlout violated Parliament's conflict of interest code, but recommended against imposing any penalties against her.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Plane spotter or Chinese spy? Ontario university student suspected of espionage at airports
candidates.description: A University of Waterloo student is suspected of espionage after the FBI said he admitted to accessing airport facilities in Toronto and Chicago, to take photos on behalf of a shadowy figure from China. Weiheng Zeng, himself a Chinese citizen, was arrested in Michigan on Aug. 23 and charged with making false statements.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Maritime farmers hit by major drought last summer say they're on the road to recovery
candidates.description: While the impact of last year's drought still casts a lingering fear on the farmers, they find the crops looking great so far and expect a slow recovery.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian Tire and Tim Hortons join forces to link their loyalty programs
candidates.description: Under the partnership launched between the restaurant and the home goods company on Wednesday, customers who link their Triangle and Tims Rewards accounts will earn between two and five per cent in Canadian Tire money in addition to Tims points on select Tims purchases.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Teachers, students file new wave of lawsuits against OpenAI over Tumbler Ridge shooting
candidates.description: New legal filings describe the horror students and teachers experienced on Feb. 10 and include new details of OpenAI's alleged negligence in preventing the shooting.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Counter tariffs will add to 'perfect storm' of homebuilding challenges, N.L. builders say
candidates.description: Countertariffs Canada is preparing to place on more than $27 billion of American products has left a cloud of uncertainty for homebuilders in Newfoundland and Labrador, who say business could become more expensive and difficult.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Carney's 'hydronym' moment is behind a cheeky campaign to raise awareness about Lake Ontario
candidates.description: Riding on Prime Minister Mark Carney's use of the proper word for a body of water, a London, Ont., company has created T-shirts emblazoned with "My hydronyms are Lake and Ontario." A portion of the apparel sales proceeds go to Swim Drink Fish Canada, a charity that connects people with the lake, and works to keep it safe and clean.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Neskantaga First Nation's lack of health-care infrastructure forces evacuation of dozens to Toronto
candidates.description: Four weeks after Neskantaga First Nation declared a state of emergency over a sewage spill at its nursing station, a fire at the temporary health-care facility has left the community scrambling again. Officials with Indigenous Services Canada have visited the First Nation to assess the situation, which has forced the relocation of about 250 vulnerable people to Toronto.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Telus accused of misleading B.C. consumer watchdog in probe sparked by mistaken $1,400 cancellation fee
candidates.description: B.C.'s consumer watchdog is locked in a court battle with Telus after accusing the telecommunications giant of stonewalling an inspector trying to determine if a mistaken $1,435.65 contract cancellation fee was part of a bigger issue.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Swan River Valley, Man., farmers wait for relief after summer of floods
candidates.description: Some Manitoba farmers face a devastating year after extreme weather — including record-breaking flooding in the Parkland and Swan Valley — caused massive crop losses.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Students return to Saskatoon high school missing 26 classrooms after fire
candidates.description: Students at Bethlehem Catholic High School are back in class Wednesday for the first time since a fire last month — and the school day has been cut by half for most.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Thousands of Nova Scotians denied heating assistance would have qualified if not for cut
candidates.description: Nearly 8,000 applicants denied a provincial home heating rebate last winter would have qualified under previous rules, a CBC News analysis has found.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Lululemon the latest brand to bet on resale as second-hand clothing becomes big business
candidates.description: Shoppers looking to save money on Lululemon apparel have another option. The athletic wear company has launched its resale site in Canada. A 25,000 square foot processing hub in Calgary is at the center of the expansion.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Two sides in Alberta separation debate entrenched, with majority wanting to remain in Canada: poll
candidates.description: With fewer than 50 days until this October’s referendum, a new poll suggests Albertans remain entrenched in long-held positions tied to the idea of separating from Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Apple Maps follows Google, changes name of Lake Ontario to 'Lake America'
candidates.description: Apple changed the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America on the web version of its Apple Maps following U.S. President Donald ‌Trump's executive order renaming the lake. The move by Apple on Tuesday followed a decision by Alphabet late on Saturday to change the name of the lake on its Google Maps for U.S. users.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Where's Newfoundland?' ask shocked residents looking at Hilroy exercise books
candidates.description: As a new school year approaches, parents and students are out buying new school supplies — but one classroom staple has people in Newfoundland and Labrador demanding answers.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'That moment was glorious': How a Blue Rodeo hit became a rallying cry for Lake Ontario's name
candidates.description: When the lyrics of Blue Rodeo's Hasn't Hit Me Yet reverberated over the shore of Lake Ontario Saturday, they morphed into a rallying cry for Canadians following U.S. President Donald Trump's executive order to change the lake's name to "Lake America."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Reference to Indigenous peoples removed from Premier Smith's Alberta Day statement 'in error'
candidates.description: An updated version of Alberta Premier Danielle Smith's statement commemorating the province's 121st birthday was issued with the original statement's reference to Indigenous peoples removed.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Arrest warrants issued in Mexico for duo accused in alleged condo scam
candidates.description: A Mexican court has issued arrest warrants against the man and woman accused of defrauding a Canadian couple of their retirement savings through an alleged condo-flip scheme, CBC News has learned.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Jurors in trial of U.S. mother who killed her children again tell judge they are deadlocked
candidates.description: Jurors in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial have said — for a second time — that they are unable to reach a verdict on whether she is criminally responsible in the killings of her three children, but the judge on Wednesday told them again to keep trying.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The battle that made Canada bleed: Operation Medusa, 20 years later
candidates.description: It has been 20 years since Canadian soldiers walked into a Taliban killing ground west of Kandahar. Operation Medusa became Canada’s largest battle since Korea — a brutal test against a disciplined, entrenched enemy. Canada prevailed, but at a terrible cost, in a fight that changed the Afghan war and those who survived it.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Chevron expands Venezuela presence with $7B US plan
candidates.description: Chevron will invest more than $7 billion US through its Venezuela joint ventures to double oil production to about 600,000 barrels per day over the next five years in the ‌South American country, the U.S. oil major said on Wednesday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Iran attacks U.S. bases across Gulf after reports of deadly strike on wedding
candidates.description: Iran and its Arab neighbours were plunged back into war on Wednesday by the biggest exchange of fire between Tehran and Washington since July, with U.S. forces striking Iran's southern coast and Iran firing at American bases across the region.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Low flypast over Cape Town stadium to be reviewed, South Africa says
candidates.description: South Africa's aviation regulator is probing a low flypast by two jets over a Cape Town stadium last week.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Climate change past the point of no return, UN says, as worst impacts are now unavoidable
candidates.description: In a strategic retreat in the fight against climate change, the United Nations has acknowledged that Earth has lost its chance to prevent some of the worst of global warming's harms. Officials say the world must now figure out how to get temperatures below the danger zone and back to safety.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Get your rhinestones ready: Dollyfest 2027 set to honour Dolly Parton's legacy
candidates.description: Grab your glitteriest outfit and your tallest blonde wig: Dollyfest is set to go ahead in 2027 without its titular star, with the festival now transformed into a celebration of Dolly Parton’s life, her estate has announced.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Explosion near southern Germany train station injures 2
candidates.description: An explosion near a German train station followed by the discovery of a suspicious object caused police to temporarily close the transport hub in the southern city of Augsburg on Wednesday morning.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hopes of finding survivors dim a week after catastrophic Nepal flood
candidates.description: Rescue teams raced on Wednesday to reach dozens of workers believed to be trapped inside hydropower tunnels in Nepal's mountains, offering one of the last hopes of finding survivors a week after a Himalayan flood killed more than 1,200 people.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The U.S. could soon control 20% of Venezuela's oil reserves. Canada's oilpatch isn't worried
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump is continuing his pursuit of Venezuela's oil jackpot, announcing a new deal aimed at boosting production in the South American country. And while Trump is flaunting the potential controlling stake in a portion of Venezuela's oil reserves as a warning to Canada, experts say there is little cause for concern in Western Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Day of attacks by U.S. and Iran marks most serious escalation of conflict in weeks
candidates.description: The U.S. launched new air strikes on Iranian targets on ‌Tuesday, in a move that threatened to reignite the six-month-old conflict that has driven global energy prices higher and weighed heavily on U.S. President Donald Trump's popularity at home.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong pleads guilty in 2nd national security case
candidates.description: Prominent Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong pleaded guilty Wednesday to conspiracy to collude with foreign forces to endanger national security under a Beijing-imposed law that has effectively stifled the city's once-thriving pro-democracy movement.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: In search for senior Hamas operative, Israeli raid on Gaza City camp kills 3 children
candidates.description: Four people were killed in a Gaza City displacement camp Tuesday in a raid Israel's defence minister said was to locate a senior Hamas official.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Accused in Charlie Kirk shooting pleads not guilty to murder charge that could carry death penalty
candidates.description: Tyler Robinson, the man accused of fatally shooting prominent U.S. conservative activist Charlie Kirk on ‌a Utah college campus last year, pleaded not guilty on Tuesday to a murder charge that a judge ruled could carry the death penalty.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: More than 1,000 dead from catastrophic Nepal-China floods as rescuers search for survivors
candidates.description: Rescue teams with search dogs on Tuesday continued to look through mud, rocks and debris along the border between Nepal and China for thousands of people still missing following the catastrophic floods that tore through communities across the Himalayas, leaving more than 1,000 dead.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada poaches top American talent | About That
candidates.description: Canada is attracting dozens of top academics from the United States with a promise to support their work, which has been deprioritized by the Trump administration. Andrew Chang breaks down how this sweep of American professors fits into Canada's trade war with the U.S. (Photo credits: The Canadian Press, Reuters, Adobe Stock and Getty Images)
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Inflation risks rise with higher fuel costs and new U.S. tariffs, Bank of Canada governor warns
candidates.description: The Bank of Canada held its benchmark interest rate steady on Wednesday at 2.25 per cent, in a move widely expected by economists.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Unifor and Stellantis begin contract negotiations under threat of auto tariffs
candidates.description: The negotiations are the last round of bargaining between the Big Three carmakers — Stellantis, Ford and GM — and Unifor, which represents autoworkers at each. And with the backdrop of American tariffs threatening Canada's auto industry, the talks come at a critical juncture.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Lake America' change highlights Canada's reliance on U.S. tech
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump's push to rename Lake Ontario "Lake America" underscores Canada's reliance on U.S. tech giants like Google and Apple.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Grain being shipped out of Port of Churchill for 1st time in 6 years
candidates.description: A ship is set to leave the Port of Churchill this week loaded with what would be the northern Manitoba town's first grain shipment in over half a decade.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Iran says US strike killed four at wedding in 'war crime' as US denies targeting civilians
candidates.description: Iranian media reports two children were among those killed when shrapnel hit a home. Iran then launched missiles and drones at US targets in the Middle East.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Iranian attack on Saudi tanker killed two Filipino sailors, Saudi Arabia says
candidates.description: The kingdom condemns the targeting of Sidr, which was reportedly hit by unknown projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: EU and Nato vow to step up pressure on Russia after 'new escalation' in Germany
candidates.description: Russia is accused of growing increasingly reckless after Berlin blamed Russia for a failed drone attack on Leipzig airport.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US sailors arrive in Thailand's Pattaya after record 250 days at sea
candidates.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln is docking close to Pattaya, known for its neon-lit nightlife, and for sex tourism.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Woman charged with juror intimidation in Lindsay Clancy trial
candidates.description: Dawn Light is accused of taking photos of jurors outside the Plymouth courthouse, a practice prohibited by the court.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Zelensky says airlines should avoid Russian airspace as Ukraine escalates drone operations
candidates.description: Chinese and Gulf state airlines are among those still using Russian airspace. Meanwhile, Russia says it will intensify its own attacks on Ukraine.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: More than 900 killed in Gaza this year despite ceasefire, Hamas-run health ministry says
candidates.description: The ministry says the total number of people killed in the Strip since 10 October is now more than 1,300, including 301 children.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Nepal intensifies relief and recovery efforts after deadly floods, UN says
candidates.description: More than 1,200 people have died and thousands are missing, as rescue efforts continue and aid is airlifted to villages.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Lizzo 'grateful' after judge dismisses lawsuit against production company
candidates.description: The About Damn Time singer says she is "relieved" at the outcome and will "continue to fight" every claim.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: BBC travels inside occupied Lebanon as officials say Israel expanding positions
candidates.description: A BBC team joined a humanitarian mission of the UN peacekeeping force, which says Israeli troops are fortifying positions and continuing demolitions.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Ariana Grande makes emotional tour exit and steps back from public life
candidates.description: The star makes an emotional farewell as she wraps up a tour she's described as her "last hurrah".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Remarkable US oil deal puzzles analysts - and angers many Venezuelans
candidates.description: Amounting to 65 billion barrels of crude, the deal is labelled by one ex-envoy as a colonialist "fever dream".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Could the man who murdered a Christian missionary and his sons walk free in India?
candidates.description: Dara Singh is serving a life sentence for burning alive Graham Staines and his two sons in Odisha in 1999.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'I've never been to Afghanistan': Six million deportees forced to start over under the Taliban
candidates.description: As of August, the number forced to return this year from Pakistan and Iran had reached another million.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Pistol in a lake gives hope for French cold case
candidates.description: Saad al-Hilli was shot dead with his wife and mother-in-law while holidaying in eastern France in September 2012.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'Nothing but mud and silt' - the village swept away by deadly floods in Nepal
candidates.description: BBC South Asia correspondent Azadeh Moshiri spoke to a local, who is still waiting for his his wife's body to be retrieved, as rescue efforts continue.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Why US troops have a history in this raucous Thai city
candidates.description: The BBC's Jonathan Head looks at the historical echoes of US troops arriving in Pattaya, a beach resort famous for its racy bars.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Norway's new king takes oath as mourners pay respects to his late father
candidates.description: Norway's new King takes the first major step of his reign as his father, the late King Harald V, lies in state at the Royal Palace.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Moment Duane 'Keffe D' Davis is found guilty of Tupac Shakur's murder
candidates.description: The rapper's killing became one of popular culture's great mysteries, with countless theories but no arrests until 2023.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Orangutans in danger as wildfires blaze through Borneo
candidates.description: Wildfires in Indonesia have destroyed part of the natural habitat of hundreds of orangutans, risking the survival of the species.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Lords call for AI 'kill switch' powers in UK
candidates.description: Its backers say it would provide a "vital safety net" against runaway AI systems such as those from OpenAI and Anthropic.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Fake 10 Downing Street listing exposes 'unfit' Booking.com, says consumer group
candidates.description: Booking.com said the "limited test" was "not a true reflection of the experience of millions of listings or reviews".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: AI could cause global economic downturn, Andrew Bailey warns G20
candidates.description: The governor of the Bank of England warned of AI's “volatility” caused by energy shocks from the US-Iran war.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Astronauts set out on rare all-female spacewalk
candidates.description: For the sixth time in history, a team of two women completed a spacewalk outside the International Space Station.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How a small island in Canada appeared, vanished, and was found again
candidates.description: Officials in British Columbia say the floating island drifted towards the shoreline of a local lake. But its origins remain a mystery.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Met Office: Summer 2026 was UK's hottest ever
candidates.description: The UK had a spring and summer of persistent heat with five widespread heatwaves and 40 days of temperatures above 30C (86F), smashing the previous record of 34 days.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Summer 2026 was UK's hottest on record, Met Office says
candidates.description: Met Office figures show that the previous record, set in 2025, has been broken after an unprecedented summer of persistent heat.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: New storm names for 2026-2027 released by Met Office
candidates.description: Tuesday 1 September marks the start of the UK storm season and a new list of storm names have been released including Austen, Chloe and Evelyn.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Astronauts set out on rare all-female spacewalk
candidates.description: For the sixth time in history, a team of two women completed a spacewalk outside the International Space Station.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'We'll find way to save Jodrell Bank,' Burnham says
candidates.description: Burnham said "there is no way that we can see its demise, and it won't happen under my Government".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Iran fires on its Gulf neighbors, retaliating for U.S. strikes after a monthlong lull
candidates.description: The six-month war has led to a spike in oil prices, roiled the global economy and posed increasing political problems for President Trump's Republican Party ahead of November midterm elections.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Greetings from the Royal Pavilion, a stunning reminder of India in southern England
candidates.description: Looking up at this 18th century building, it became clear the British didn't only bring their architectural style to India. They also took some of India's style home.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Chevron to expand in Venezuela, days after the U.S. and Venezuela strike oil deal
candidates.description: Chevron is the largest foreign oil operator in Venezuela. The deal will expand its footprint at a time of political and economic uncertainty for Venezuela.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: India's prime minister is wooing the Gen Z while cracking down on them
candidates.description: Over two months, protesters, most who appeared to be digitally-savvy GenZ, used social media to organize. Government's efforts to respond spotlight how the ruling party appears to be playing catch-up.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: ICE says it now has enough body cameras. And, Congress averts shutdown before midterms
candidates.description: Immigration and Customs Enforcement says it now has enough body cameras to equip all of its agents. And, Congress votes to fund the government, averting a government shutdown ahead of the midterms.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Israel bars U.S. citizens over criticism and ties to Palestinian activists, lawyers say
candidates.description: Travelers from the U.S. and other nations are denied entry to Israel after interrogations about their links to Palestinians, plans to visit the occupied West Bank and opinions of Israel, lawyers say.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Germany blames Russia for last month's attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport
candidates.description: The German government blamed Russia for an attempted attack at Leipzig airport last month using a drone laden with explosives. It announced that it would shut down a Russian consulate among measures.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Putin signals support for Iran in ongoing war with the U.S.
candidates.description: Russia's Vladimir Putin is signaling unwavering support for Iran, as Tehran thanks Moscow for backing amid the escalating Middle East war.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Who is Betancourt, the man behind the company the US is partnering with in Venezuela?
candidates.description: The man behind the company that the US is partnering with in Venezuela is Alejandro Betancourt. He has faced multiple investigations in Spain, the United States and Switzerland for money laundering.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.S. military strikes Iran, while Trump vows more for Tehran's retaliation
candidates.description: The U.S. military hit targets in Iran on Tuesday and Tehran fired missiles and drones at various sites across the region in response as hostilities flare once again in an intermittent war.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: New lawsuits claim OpenAI execs put image ahead of safety in Canadian mass shooting
candidates.description: The suits say that recommendations to alert police about the alleged shooter were nixed by OpenAI's global affairs team, led by veteran political strategist Chris Lehane. OpenAI denies the claims.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Kalshi bans former congressman George Santos for life after State of the Union trades
candidates.description: Kalshi says Santos did not cooperate with its investigation into bets he placed on his own attendance at the State of the Union. The company also fined the disgraced congressman more than $71,000.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The U.S. sues Amazon again
candidates.description: Federal regulators and 22 states allege that the tech giant made billions by manipulating how much brands and sellers paid for ads on its platform.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Medical groups offer vaccine guidance to fill federal vacuum
candidates.description: In the unprecedented absence of federal guidance, leading medical groups are issuing their own recommendations for who should get the COVID-19, flu and RSV immunizations.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Whatever happened to ... children infected with HIV due to failures in healthcare?
candidates.description: For years, Pakistan has seen cases of children infected with HIV due to unsafe treatment in clinics and hospitals. A current outbreak numbers hundreds of cases. Why does this problem keep occurring?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Dry eyes are common among women. Here's why you shouldn't ignore it
candidates.description: Dry eyes are a very common chronic eye condition among women in perimenopause and beyond. Here's why you shouldn't ignore it.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: They live by a shrine to a saint. Why are their homes being demolished?
candidates.description: The neighborhood is a pilgrimage site, with a shrine to the Sufi saint known as Bari Imam. In the past year, hundreds of homes of the working poor were razed. Residents fear more will be demolished.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A N.Y. hospital tried to close its birthing center. This city united to fight back
candidates.description: Democrats and Republicans in Troy, N.Y., took on a national Catholic health system and kept the county's last birthing center open.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Whatever happened to the U.S. famine alert system that Trump shut down, then reopened
candidates.description: The highly regarded FEWS NET network stopped posting data on Afghanistan, Somalia and Yemen -- then says it will start posting again in September. What's the reason for this back-and-forth?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: NPR's 2-year search for the truth about deaths from heat
candidates.description: An investigation from NPR and Boston University finds that heat kills thousands of Americans every year. But official numbers radically undercount heat deaths.

candidates.title: Beyond Scores: Understanding LLM-as-a-Judge Mechanisms in Summarization Evaluation
candidates.description: LLM-based evaluators of natural language generation (NLG) quality are widely deployed as scoring tools and as automated training signals, yet the internal procedure by which they assign a rating remains poorly understood. We investigate this procedure mechanistically through an eight-attack perturbation taxonomy across the Readability and Adequacy dimensions of NLG quality, a generation pipeline that produces paired clean and corrupt summaries with controlled error intensity and explicit token-level modification maps, and a four-experiment battery of causal tracing, logit-lens vocabulary projection, and attention-head knockout applied to Themis (Llama-3-8B) and Prometheus (Mistral-7B). Both evaluators implement a structured, coherent evaluation pipeline operating in two stages: below layer 15, attention performs local error comparison and routes the result to the final input position; above it, the MLP cascade integrates the signal and writes the rating, with the decision crystallizing in the residual stream at a sharp late layer (L = 26 on Themis, L = 25 on Prometheus). Furthermore, a base-model control at the same scale (Llama-3-8B) reproduces the routing architecture and crystallization but not the stage separation, isolating the two mechanisms that fine-tuning specifically installs, suppression of below-L15 MLP contribution at the last position and a two-layer advance of the crystallization depth, indicating that fine-tuning sculpts an existing substrate rather than building the pipeline from scratch. We release the source code and data at https://github.com/himil-v/judge-mech
candidates.author: Himil Vasava, Ming Jiang

candidates.title: Efficient SWE Agent Benchmarking via Trajectory-Aware Evaluation
candidates.description: Evaluating software engineering agents on realistic benchmarks is costly, since each task may require multi-step code exploration, modification, and test execution. Existing efficient evaluation methods select representative subsets to estimate full-benchmark performance, but are largely result-only: they fit historical pass/fail response matrices or static task semantics, discarding how agents solve problems. We propose PTA-IRT, a Privileged Trajectory-Aware Item Response Theory framework that fuses process and outcome signals. Historical execution trajectories supply process-level evidence beyond pass/fail, such as explored context, attempted edits, and solving paths, which PTA-IRT uses as privileged information for calibration subset selection and ability estimation. Under low calibration budgets, PTA-IRT consistently outperforms prior IRT baselines on score and ranking recovery across four SWE benchmarks. Code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/DeepSoftwareAnalytics/PTA-IRT.
candidates.author: Kefeng Duan, Dewu Zheng, Yanlin Wang, Xiwen Wang, Ensheng Shi, Xilin Liu, Yuchi Ma, Jiachi Chen, Mingwei Liu, Zibin Zheng

candidates.title: Adaptive Critical Token-Aware Retrieval for Repository-Level Code Generation
candidates.description: The repository-level code generation task requires synthesizing code that satisfies task requirements while remaining consistent with the target repository context. Since real-world repositories often exceed the input length limits of LLMs, existing approaches commonly adopt retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to provide repository-specific context. Despite improving repository-context retrieval, existing methods typically provide context as task-level support, without explicitly identifying the critical tokens that require fine-grained repository context during generation. During the autoregressive generation process of LLMs, errors often concentrate at a small number of decisive positions: once such tokens are generated incorrectly, subsequent code may follow an incorrect semantic path and eventually lead to functional failure. We refer to these positions as "critical tokens". In this paper, we propose ACToR, an adaptive critical token-aware retrieval framework for repository-level code generation. ACToR identifies critical tokens during generation and triggers targeted retrieval on demand to provide repository context at these decisive positions. In addition, we design a position-aware weighting method for dense retrievers to prioritize context that is more informative for generation. We evaluate ACToR on two representative repository-level benchmarks, RepoExec and CoderEval. Experimental results show that ACToR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving relative improvements of 8.4% on RepoExec and 15.4% on CoderEval. Beyond performance gains, we systematically quantify the impact of critical tokens, revealing their central role in major generation failures and highlighting the necessity of targeted retrieval strategies. We provide the code and data at https://github.com/DeepSoftwareAnalytics/ACToR.
candidates.author: Kefeng Duan, Dewu Zheng, Yanlin Wang, Terry Yue Zhuo, Mingwei Liu, Jianxing Yu, Jiachi Chen, Ensheng Shi, Xilin Liu, Yuchi Ma, Zibin Zheng

candidates.title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?
candidates.description: Dynamic agent harnesses let language models change the software that shapes their own execution. This flexibility brings a new reasoning burden: a local plugin change can propagate through dependencies and cleanup. We introduce CordisBench, a 1,200-question benchmark of this lifecycle reasoning. It combines a controlled formal setting with programs executed against Cordis, a runtime that manages component dependencies and cleanup, and asks models to identify affected components, predict state after a specified teardown order, determine which conditions hold under all or some orders, and choose reconfigurations that succeed when executed. Across these tasks, we evaluate three efficiency-oriented models at low reasoning effort with 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, or 32 relevant interactions, using deterministic task-specific scoring. Models usually handle small systems well but grow less reliable as more interactions become relevant, especially when predicting final state and when reasoning across teardown orders. Additional inference effort recovers marked gains for some models. The cost is nontrivial: on our 16-interaction subset, GPT-5.6 Luna uses nearly 3,000 reasoning tokens per question at medium effort. For these controlled instances, that cost is avoidable: an independent finite reference semantics agrees with Cordis execution on every observation and action outcome used for scoring across all 528 executable questions.
candidates.author: Damien Sileo, Dimitri Kachler

candidates.title: The Rise of Verbal Reinforcement Learning
candidates.description: Natural language is emerging as a primary feedback channel for improving language agents, capable of conveying intent, preferences, and causal structure in forms interpretable by both humans and modern language models. We call this paradigm Verbal Reinforcement Learning (VRL) and offer the first unified account of it. We organize the field around a single axis, \textit{when} verbal feedback takes effect in an agent's lifecycle and \textit{what} it modifies, yielding three pillars: (1) \textbf{Language as Grounding Signal}, where language defines the task itself by specifying goals, states, and reward structures; (2) \textbf{Language as Deliberative Feedback}, where natural language guides reasoning at test time without the need to update model parameters; (3) \textbf{Language as Learning Signal}, where language-based feedback shapes model parameters through training. Within each pillar, we synthesize representative work, distinguish key subcategories of approaches, and outline the distinct role language plays in shaping agent behavior. Together, this taxonomy shows how verbal reinforcement is reshaping agent development, while also defining the challenges and opportunities for building more capable and aligned agents.
candidates.author: Kshitij Tayal, Arun Sharma, Genta Indra Winata, Anirban Das, Sambit Sahu

candidates.title: Facet-0: A Robotic Foundation Model for Contact-Rich Precise Manipulation
candidates.description: Real-world robotic assembly at sub-millimeter tolerances demands spatial precision, compliant interaction, and robustness to contact failures. We present Facet-0, a robotic foundation model that predicts and values the contact consequences of its actions. Facet-0 unifies multimodal representation learning and reinforcement learning (RL) post-training around a joint action-wrench proposal: a causal wrench history is aligned with vision-language semantics and kinematic state, and flow matching generates each action chunk together with the future wrist-wrench profile it is expected to induce. Deployment rollouts train a distributional Action-Wrench Critic to distinguish motions with similar task progress but different contact outcomes, while phase-aware rewards and contact-selective credit concentrate policy improvement on decisive interactions. To accommodate part-specific dynamics, a lightweight bounded actor reuses the frozen representation for on-robot adaptation; RL remains defined over executable Cartesian actions, while an auxiliary wrench head preserves predictive, non-commanded action-contact coupling. Trained on ManuFacet-1K, a 1,000-hour force-synchronized corpus spanning three embodiments and multiple manufacturing cells, the bounded task-adapted system reaches 82% mean success on five sub-millimeter computer-assembly tasks, compared with 15% for the strongest baseline, with 0.5 mm placement accuracy and 50 ms command latency.
candidates.author: Haoyuan Deng, Haichao Liu, Wenkai Guo, Yuan Ling, Zaijia Yang, Yuanjiang Xue, Haosheng Sun, Liangzi Wang, Ziwei Wang

candidates.title: Mechanism Design for Alignment and Control
candidates.description: We develop a framework for mechanism design with AI agents whose alignment (preferences) and capabilities (feasible actions and information) are unknown. We want such agents to act on our behalf so mechanisms must incentivize both honesty and obedience. A one-sided imitation structure---capabilities can be concealed but not counterfeited---yields a revelation principle, a characterization of implementable policies via nested cyclical monotonicity, and conditions under which eliciting higher-order beliefs can discipline multiple agents. We apply our framework to stylized examples of (i) sandbagging in which a more capable agent pretends to be less capable; (ii) an alignment--interpretability trade-off, where the two are substitutes in the instrument but complements in value; (iii) discipline via peer scoring; (iv) coupling rewards to induce competition among multiple agents; and (v) scalable oversight and reward shaping.
candidates.author: Dirk Bergemann, Andrew Koh, Stephen Morris

candidates.title: StudentSim: Training LLM-based Student Simulators
candidates.description: AI tutors are most useful when they adapt to each student's strengths, weaknesses, and preferred guidance, but evidence about which guidance works for which student is sparse, slow, and costly to collect from real learners. Student simulators can provide this signal as a proxy, yet existing approaches are limited: state-tracking models fit student behavior but struggle to process explanations or corrections, while LLM role-play follows guidance fluently but does not reliably match the competence of the student being imitated. We present StudentSim, a training framework that turns sparse per-student data into individualized simulators through pooled training followed by per-student specialization. The resulting simulators both mirror a student's own responses and update them under tutor guidance. We also introduce StudentSimEval, a standardized protocol covering 60 students across chess, second-language English writing, and mathematics, using public learner datasets with de-identified records shared for research. StudentSimEval measures behavioral fidelity (F), or how well a simulator matches a student's responses, and guidance responsiveness (R), or how readily it updates under tutor guidance, with all methods fit and evaluated on the same records. Across all three domains, StudentSim outperforms GPT-5.4 on both metrics. In chess, StudentSim reaches F=0.51 and R=0.91, compared with 0.23 and 0.72 for GPT-5.4 and 0.45 and 0.27 for Maia2. As a proof of concept, using StudentSim as a reward model for tutor reinforcement learning produces a chess tutor that expert humans rate as more accurate, better-guided, and more personalized than a no-RL baseline and a tutor trained against a GPT-5.4 simulator reward. Code is available at https://github.com/microsoft/StudentSim.
candidates.author: Ke Yang, Chenglong Wang, Michel Galley, Chandan Singh, Jeevana Priya Inala, ChengXiang Zhai, Jianfeng Gao

candidates.title: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing
candidates.description: Writing involves diverse cognitive activities, from ideation to revision, and writers' needs vary across individuals and moments. Proactive AI promises to provide the right support at the right time, yet existing proactive tools largely focus on generic textual assistance, such as autocomplete. This paper studies the design space of proactive thought partners: AI agents that proactively offer customizable, higher-level cognitive support during writing. We instantiated this concept in a technology probe and deployed it with 16 participants for one week. The probe allows users to create partners by configuring their roles and proactivity. As users write, relevant partners take the initiative at appropriate moments to offer suggestions. Our findings show that participants configured proactive support through prospective planning, used suggestions for both idea generation and self-monitoring, and valued lightweight visual representations alongside non-directive rhetorical framing for non-intrusive interventions. We derive implications for designing proactive writing assistants around customization, timing, engagement, and representation.
candidates.author: Chao Zhang, Abe Davis, Chih-Wei Chen, Chin-Chia Hsu

candidates.title: The Structure of Quantization Damage in LLMs: Why the Next Bit Should Be Spent Globally
candidates.description: Post-training quantization (PTQ) is widely used to reduce the cost of serving large language models (LLMs), but its accuracy cost is uneven and is often tuned per model. We study where quantization damage occurs and how to allocate a small additional precision budget. Using causal mixed-precision intervention as ground truth (raise each layer to 8-bit in turn and measure the accuracy it recovers) across 9 open-weight models in 4 architecture families, we test 3 intuitive hypotheses: that quantization damage lives in task circuits, where the model computes, or in weight statistics. None of them predicts which layers benefit from restored precision. Recovery is instead diffuse: for 8 of 9 models, recovering 75% of the gap takes roughly half the layers; the lone exception, Qwen3-8B, is sharply concentrated. At a matched precision budget, spending it globally on finer quantization granularity beats locally repairing the most recoverable layers for all 8 group-128-compatible models (all but OpenLLaMA, whose width rules out group-128), by 21-52 points, including the concentrated Qwen3-8B. We report 2 secondary findings: the residual is budget-limited (8-bit is near-lossless in our evaluation across RTN, GPTQ, and AWQ), and the location of peak recovery correlates with architecture within a family, though not across families. Within this budget setting, global granularity is a better default than selectively protecting critical layers. More broadly, cheap signals that correlate with quantization damage do not necessarily identify where restoring precision improves accuracy; this must be tested with causal intervention.
candidates.author: Jundong Hu, Shekar Ramachandran

candidates.title: SG-AMP: Scene-Graph-Guided Active Perception and Semantics-Aware Motion Planning for Pepper Plants
candidates.description: We present SG-AMP, integrating robust depth completion with input-conditioned uncertainty, persistent panoptic mapping, plant scene-graph reasoning, and semantics-aware active view-motion planning. Beyond inspecting uncertain observed regions, the scene graph explicitly hypothesizes unobserved pepper--peduncle attachments and directs close-range sensing toward them. Candidate views are selected according to expected information gain, while class-dependent motion costs distinguish protected peppers, peduncles, and stems from conditionally traversable foliage. On pepper data, the perception network achieves $55.27\%$ semantic mIoU, $38.67\%$ PQ, and $40.62\,\mathrm{mm}$ depth RMSE, while input-conditioned uncertainty improves NYUv2 NLL from $-1.6518$ to $-1.6925$ and AUSE from $0.0102$ to $0.0087$.
candidates.author: Rohit Menon, Shiva Rudra Lolla, Niklas Mueller-Goldingen, Gokul Chenchani, Ribana Roscher, Maren Bennewitz

candidates.title: Closing Cost-Quality Gap in Document VLMs: Difficulty-Aware Data Curation and Quality-Adjusted Deployment Economics
candidates.description: Extracting structured fields from hundreds of millions of documents annually remains costly in regulated industries: bespoke OCR cascades cover only a fraction of workflows, privacy rules preclude external models, and existing open-source VLMs that clear quality thresholds cost more to serve than human annotation. We present a deployed document-understanding system built on a Mixture-of-Experts VLM (35B total, 3B active), fine-tuned on in-house production data mixed with open-domain documents curated by a Difficulty-Aware pipeline for layout diversity, fact-extractability, and cross-model consistency. Fitting on a single H100 and serving heterogeneous workflows via prompting, the model leads all deployable (non-reasoning) baselines up to an order of magnitude larger. A quality-adjusted cost analysis, with confirmation and correction costs calibrated from production telemetry, shows it reduces expected costs by over 80% against the human baseline and by more than 50% against the best competing open-source model, while larger baselines remain economically unviable.
candidates.author: Maksim Evdokimov, Matvey Ivanov, Dmitrii Tsiupin, Olga Tsymboi, Anatolii Potapov, Aleksandr Ivanov
